Articulation Agreement Overview

This agreement outlines lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Students are strongly encouraged to consult an academic advisor to ensure they meet all degree requirements for their intended baccalaureate program.


Helpful Resources:

  • CSUB Catalog
  • Transfer Admission Requirements

Course Equivalency Information for 4-Year Institutions

Students and staff can explore course transfer equivalencies through the Transfer Evaluation System (TES). Equivalency agreements are updated regularly and subject to change. For the most current information, please refer to TES or contact the Articulation Office.

","groupId":"dd266645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"About the Major","groupId":"de266645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

The program in Anthropology administers one degree, a Bachelor of Arts. Students have the option of adding a concentration in Cultural Resource Management, which is designed to enhance the field training, laboratory analysis, heritage management laws, and applied skills necessary for employment in this rapidly growing field of professional applied anthropology and historic preservation.

The Anthropology program faculty stresses a close working relationship with students and strongly encourages students to take full advantage of the many opportunities the department provides for collaborative research with faculty, student internships, and other direct collaboration of professional skills.


For additional information, visit the following:

Department of Anthropology
